root_idea.summary: The root denotes diminution: making something deficient or causing it to lose its increase or blessing.
root_idea.development: Its semantic range extends from decrease and loss of blessing to disappearance or total effacement; the lunar noun applies the image of waning to the end of the month.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form مَحَقَ rather than the imperfect QAC lemma يَمْحَقُ.

senses.definition: To diminish or reduce something, especially by removing its increase or blessing.
senses.usage_conditions: In the construction يَمْحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبَا, the object is made deficient and deprived of its increase or blessing.

senses.definition: To efface, annihilate, or destroy something completely, leaving no trace.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَيَمْحَقَ الْكَافِرِينَ, the focus is the result of complete destruction or obliteration rather than mere diminution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Diminution, depletion, or loss of increase and blessing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun naming the state or act expressed by مَحَقَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The waning or disappearance of the moon at the end of the lunar month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for the final lunar phase and in the expression لَيَالِي الْمِحَاقِ, the nights of that waning phase.
